[7] The department provides training in cultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology, archaeology, and physical anthropology. [11] While it is a traditional four-field department, the graduate program allows students to engage in research across subdisciplines. [11] The program also features highly-regarded subdisciplinary specialties like medical anthropology and forensic anthropology. [11] Graduate education in Anthropology at MSU aims to cultivate high scholarly achievement in the next generation of anthropologists, emphasizing a commitment to research, public engagement, and the ethical practice of the discipline. [11] The department values the diversity of its scholarly community and is dedicated to maintaining and supporting this diversity. It also stresses the importance of collaborative work with the communities being studied and the need to share research with various audiences. [14] The program of study is planned by the student in consultation with the major professor and a guidance committee. [8] Specific courses in biochemistry, as well as courses in other areas considered relevant to the student's interests and chosen research area, are included in the program. [8] The major objectives of the graduate programs in BMB are to help students to develop their creative potential and to prepare them for careers in research and teaching in the biochemical sciences. [14] It is expected that the dissertation will show original treatment of an important research problem, will give evidence of independent thought, and will be clearly, logically, and carefully written. [8] It is also expected that the research on which the dissertation is based will be published in the scientific literature. [8]

The program is characterized by its interdisciplinary and interinstitutional perspectives on problems and issues of educational practice, as well as its commitment to educational justice and to addressing critical challenges faced by children, students, families, and communities. The program combines internationally renowned faculty, an interdisciplinary approach, exposure to multiple ideas, and flexibility in study through a variety of focal areas to create a one-of-a-kind learning experience tailored to students' goals and commitments. The program is designed to facilitate doctoral students' enactment of the Departments Core Principles in their scholarship, teaching, and service/outreach. [7]
Accredidation: The Michigan State University College of Education Educator Preparation Programs are accredited under the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) standards. [3] The current accreditation approval is from May 2022 to June 2029. [3] Additionally, Michigan State University as a whole is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [7]

ProgramName: Certificate in Higher Education Administration Enrollment Management
Certificate in Higher Education Administration Student Life & Development
Requirements: Admission to all graduate programs in the School of Education and Human Development is based on the recommendation of the faculty. Admissions decisions are based on faculty review of the following general requirements that apply to all Graduate Programs in the School as well as specific documents listed under each concentration. Applicants must: a master’s degree from an accredited institution;; Provide three letters of recommendation that address the issues and meet the criteria established by the program being Applied To; provide a personal statement that addresses the mission and purpose of the program being applied to;; Provide a current resume;; Take part in an admission interview (required by some programs); and; Exhibit personal and professional experiences and characteristics that are relevant to the profession and/or field and/or program for which the application is being submitted. [4]

ProgramName: Certificate in Historic Preservation
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Historic Preservation is designed for students who are interested in the preservation of historic and cultural resources, from individual buildings and sites to cultural landscapes, and who are enrolled in a master's or doctoral program at Michigan State University. The certificate program introduces students to the history and theory of historic preservation and to the methods and techniques of preservation practice. The program is administered by the Department of Art, Art History, and Design.

ProgramName: Certificate in Hospitality Design
Requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate Program is subject to the rules, regulations and procedures of the Graduate School as stipulated in the University Graduate Bulletin. [1] Applications will be reviewed by the Architecture Faculty Graduate Admissions Committee only after fulfilling the below requirements and all of the following documents have been received: Bachelor degree with a 3.0 cumulative point average (GPA), Completed application form with an application fee, A letter or statement expressing your interest in the certificate and reasons for applying, Official transcripts of all college and university courses taken, indicating the date your professional or other undergraduate degree was awarded, Three academic (and professional, if applicable) letters of recommendation, and a Digital portfolio. [1, 3]

ProgramName: Certificate in Leadership
Requirements: Applicants for the Graduate Certificate in Leadership & Managing Teams must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. [3, 8] A cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 is preferred. [8] Additionally, a minimum of three years of full-time managerial experience in a supervisory role is strongly preferred. [3, 4] Other admission requirements include demonstrating potential for organizational leadership and possessing attributes like strong communication skills, analytical thinking, and leadership qualities. [3] Submitted application items must include a completed application form with a nonrefundable fee, official transcripts from all previously attended colleges or universities (excluding Michigan State University), a current resume, three letters of recommendation, and a statement of intention essay. [3]
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Leadership and Managing Teams focuses on the universal themes of managers from any organization: effective leadership and team management, negotiation, and organizational design and development. [6] This online certificate is designed to meet the needs of working professionals from a wide variety of fields and backgrounds while focusing on a broad spectrum of skill sets including team design and dynamics, managing diversity, and creating an ethical organization. [6] The curriculum incorporates applicable concepts and strategies for negotiations, communications and designing an organizational structure that works for you. [3] It provides methods to help you develop your own leadership style, as well as techniques for promoting an ethical workplace. [3]

ProgramName: Certificate in Legal Aspects of the Music Business (Online)
Requirements: A bachelor's degree is required to enroll in this certificate program. [2]
ScholarshipType: The program is eligible for Financial Aid. [4]

ProgramName: Certificate in Liberal Studies
Certificate in Media Management
Requirements:
A baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution.

ProgramName: Certificate in Second Language Acquisition and Teaching
Requirements: To be accepted to this program, you must have: A bachelor's degree. Previous work experience preferred (Résumé/CV) TOEFL/IELTS if English is not your native language and/or writing sample demonstrating advanced English language proficiency, if your prior schooling was not conducted in English. A written personal statement summarizing your background and interest in the program. An academic statement summarizing your prior schooling and preparation for graduate coursework. 3 letters of recommendation. [13]
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Second Language Studies, administered by the Department of Linguistics, Languages and Cultures, is designed to provide working professionals in applied linguistics or a related field or current graduate students at Michigan State University with materials and methodologies for researching their own practices, their program's practices, or external language-teaching programs' practices in second, additional, or multilingual language-teaching methods. [3] The foci of the program is on applied linguistics and second language acquisition, exploration of the cognitive and social mechanisms underpinning second, additional, and multilingual language development, and how identities and ideologies, and educational language policies, practices, and assessment, affect teaching and learning. [3] The program aids in the understanding of second language acquisition theory and places emphasis on including marginalized and underrepresented language learners and teachers in research on second, additional, and multilingual language learning and teaching. [3]

ProgramName: Certificate in Security Management
Requirements: Application requirements are program-specific. The Michigan State University Graduate School directs applicants to the individual program pages for a list of required materials. [22, 25, 26]
Description: To obtain the certificate, students must successfully complete the following coursework: CJ 885 - Security Management (3 Credits); CJ 886 - Security Administration (3 Credits). and one of the following: CJ 809 - Issues in Criminal Justice: Public/Private Partnerships in Emergency Preparedness and Homeland Security (3 Credits); CJ 890 - Independent Study (3 Credits). [7]

ProgramName: Post-Graduate Certificate in Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner
Post-Graduate Certificate in Adult-Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner
Post-Graduate Certificate in Family Nurse Practitioner
Requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant must: submit a university application and a curriculum vita or resume; have completed a graduate degree in Nursing from an accredited college or university; possess a current unrestricted license to practice nursing as a registered nurse in the applicant's state or country (and in Michigan if practicing there); possess current certification from a U.S. National Certifying Board as an NP, CNS, CRNA or CNM; have a minimum grade-point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the graduate nursing program; submit a written essay on career goals and motivations; submit three letters of recommendation; and complete an admission interview. ProgramName: Post-Graduate Certificate in Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing
Description: This Graduate Certificate Program is designed to prepare nurses to assume primary care roles as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner. The certificate provides nurses with essential knowledge and skills to assume psychotherapy, consultation, and liaison roles. [14] Courses focus on systematic pathophysiology, pharmacotherapeutics interventions, advanced health assessment, and health policy and issues for advanced practice nurses. [14]
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing, master's degree program in nursing and doctor of nursing practice program at Michigan State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Accounting
Requirements: To be admitted to the Accounting major, students must have been admitted to the Broad College of Business and meet the requirements for admission to the upper division. The number of students admitted to the major is limited.
Description: The Department of Accounting and Information Systems provides a Bachelor of Science degree with a major in accounting. The undergraduate accounting student follows a rigorous course of study that includes financial accounting theory and practice, cost and managerial analysis, individual and corporate income taxation, auditing concepts and issues, and accounting information systems. Students receive technical accounting skills, exposure to business analytics and communication training. The program provides an excellent foundation in accounting. Students, who complete the program along with the offered government and not-for-profit accounting course, meet the State of Michigan educational requirements to sit for the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) exam in Michigan.
Accredidation: The Broad College has been accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) since 1953. [16] AACSB International accreditation represents the highest standard of achievement for business schools worldwide. [16]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Acting
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Acting for Stage, Screen, and New Media is by audition and interview, which occurs during the spring semester of each academic year. [7]
Concentration: Acting for Stage, Screen, and New Media
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Acting for Stage, Screen, and New Media is designed for students wishing to prepare for a professional career in acting. The BFA in Acting provides highly focused course work devoted to professional and practical skill development. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science
Requirements:
To be considered for admission to the major, the student must have:
a cumulative grade-point average of at least 3.0 in all courses taken at MSU.
a minimum grade-point average of 3.0 in MTH 132, MTH 133, and MTH 234 or equivalent courses.
a minimum average of 3.0 in the grades in MTH 360 and STT 441. [3]
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science is an interdisciplinary program administered by the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics and Probability. It provides students with comprehensive training for a career in actuarial science. The curriculum reflects the interdisciplinary nature of the field and is designed to prepare students for the preliminary examinations of the Society of Actuaries (SOA) and the Casualty Actuarial Society (CAS). [4] The program also helps students acquire skills in computing, communication, and work experience that are sought by employers. [4] It is intended for students who wish to work in insurance companies, banks, investment firms, government, hospitals, and other businesses where there is a need to evaluate the financial consequences of risk. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Advertising Creative
Requirements: Enrollment in the advertising creative program is limited. In addition to the university and college requirements, students must complete Advertising 205, and Psychology 101 with a combined minimum grade–point average of 2.00. [3]
Description: The undergraduate advertising creative program prepares students to work in advertising and related industries, as art directors, designers and/or copywriters. [2] Promotional communication businesses, like advertising, demand a variety of skilled employees, including those who develop the messaging strategy, those who study the intended audience for the message, those who decide the best channel of communication to reach that audience, and those who actually compose the look, the wording and, if appropriate, the sounds of the message. [2] The advertising creative program is focused on those who actually create the advertisement. [2] Students receive a broad liberal arts background, as well as a strong overview of the advertising process that provides them with an understanding of the strategy, research, and other functions necessary to effective advertising. [2] However, greater depth of training is dedicated to helping students develop advertising art direction, design and copywriting skills. [2] Over the course of the program, students develop a portfolio of their work, to help them in seeking employment upon graduation. [2] These skills enable students to find work not only in advertising, but also in the fields of direct marketing, sales promotion, public relations, app and web design, electronic commerce, and more. [2] Internships and other cooperative educational opportunities are encouraged in the program. Co-curricular activities include multiple student clubs, as well as national student competitions. [2] Study abroad programs provide ways for students to gain experience that enhance and reach outside of the classroom, further advancing their employment opportunities. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Advertising Management
Requirements: Enrollment in the Advertising Management program is limited. In addition to the university and college requirements, students must complete Advertising 200 and Advertising 205 with a combined minimum grade–point average of 2.00. [1, 7]
Department: College of Communication Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Advertising Management provides the educational background necessary for students aspiring to become account managers, account planners, media planners, media researchers or a variety of other more managerial-oriented positions. [2] The program focuses on developing students' strategic thinking, creative problem solving, along with more research-oriented and analytical skills. [2] In this program, you will receive a broad liberal arts background, as well as a strong overview of the advertising process, providing an understanding of the strategy, research and other functions necessary to develop and manage effective advertising campaigns. [3] Internships and other cooperative educational opportunities are encouraged to broaden learning and practical experience in the major. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American and African Studies
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive. First-year admission is based on a holistic review of your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, and your leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [29] MSU strongly encourages a college preparatory curriculum in high school. [29] While there are no minimum requirements, applicants are encouraged to have four years of English, three years of mathematics (two of algebra and one of geometry), and to select honors, Advanced Placement, and International Baccalaureate courses when possible. [29] A personal statement or essay is required as part of the application. [23] Michigan State University is test-optional, meaning applicants can choose whether or not to submit an ACT or SAT score. [26]
Concentration: ['Communities in Action', 'Creative Expression, Culture and Performance', 'Black Institutions, Sustainability, and Statecraft']
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in African American and African Studies offers students the opportunity to engage and explore the lives, worlds, and cultural practices of Black peoples. Students are encouraged to study and appreciate a nuanced understanding of the diversity and complexity of Black communities as well as the particularities of Blackness as it is lived, imagined, and created. Students are also directed to the promise and possibilities of collaborative, interdisciplinary, and creative study and work and research. Multiple elements define the course of study for the major, including interconnected, required courses exploring Black Feminisms, Genders, and Sexualities Studies, as well as encouragement of diverse understandings and approaches to knowledge production with and about Black peoples.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agribusiness Management
Description: The Agribusiness Management (ABM) program focuses on system-wide business and managerial functions performed by organizations throughout the agribusiness sector. The major gives students the flexibility to choose courses related to their individual interests in farm management, commodity procurement and marketing, labor and personnel management, public policy and global food issues. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural, Food and Natural Resources Education
Requirements: First-year admission to Michigan State University is based on a holistic review of your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, and your leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [8] An essay is also a required part of the application. [16] Letters of recommendation are not required. [16]
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources
Description: MSU's teacher preparation program in Agriculture, Food and Natural Resources Education is unique in the country, with its focus on AFNR sustainability for the benefit of communities in Michigan, the U.S. and the world. Preparation of educators to teach in Agriculture, Food, Natural Resources Education (AFNRE) secondary programs requires a unique curriculum comprising a blend of pedagogy, natural science, technical agriculture and natural resource management, and community sustainability courses. [4] The educational objectives of the AFNRE program include those related to the sustainability core and those related more specifically to agricultural, food and natural resources education. For the sustainability core, the objectives are that students will demonstrate proficiency in the following areas: critical thinking, systems thinking, ecological literacy, economic literacy, boundary crossing, community, equity, civic engagement, leadership, ethics, initiative and practical skills. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Animal Science
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is based on a holistic review of academic performance in high school, curriculum strength, recent academic trends, and an essay. For the Bachelor of Science in Animal Science degree itself, the university requires the completion of 120 credits. This includes fulfilling the University's general education requirements, the requirements of the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources, and the specific course requirements for the Animal Science major. A Tier II writing requirement is also met by completing a designated course within the major. [3, 5]
ScholarshipAmount: Awards range from $500 to $3,500, with some scholarships covering full tuition and fees. [19]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, need-based, and for specific interests such as dairy, livestock production, and study abroad. [19]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology
Description: As an anthropology major at Michigan State University, you can choose to pursue either a bachelor of arts or bachelor of science degree. Both programs provide a strong liberal arts education with exposure to all subfields of anthropology while permitting you sufficient freedom to pursue secondary areas of study. [8] For either degree, you complete the standard University requirements and College of Social Science requirements in addition to a minimum of 30 credits in Anthropology Coursework. [8] You begin by taking three introductory-level classes, one introduction to cultural anthropology, one introduction to archaeology, and one introduction to physical anthropology, and one methods course. [8] In addition, you must also take one culture-area course and one thematic or analytical course. [8] Four additional courses are electives, but three of them must be at the 300-level or above. [8] To complete the major, you must take the anthropology capstone course, which also satisfies the University's Tier II writing requirement. [8] The study of anthropology contributes to the preparation of students for careers in education, medicine, business and industry, government service, and institutions in which a broad knowledge of human relations is important. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Anthropology
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University for first-year students is based on academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of the curriculum, recent academic performance trends, class rank, and ACT or SAT results. [5] MSU has a test-optional policy, allowing prospective students to apply without submitting an ACT or SAT score. [5] The university recommends a strong college preparatory curriculum, including four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies (such as anthropology), two years of science, and two years of a single foreign language. [5] For the Bachelor of Science in Anthropology major, students must complete a minimum of 33 credits in Anthropology coursework, including introductory courses in cultural anthropology, archaeology, and physical anthropology. [12, 10] Additionally, 12 credits in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) courses are required for the B.S. degree. [12]
Description: The Department of Anthropology takes culture as its central object of study, giving students a framework for viewing culture in the context of the natural world and evolutionary processes. Anthropologists also study the organization of social life, as well as symbolic and ideological systems. Anthropology views the world of human culture as a natural laboratory in which diverse historical experiments have occurred and are occurring. [10] The study of anthropology contributes to the preparation of students for careers in education, medicine, business and industry, government service, and institutions in which a broad knowledge of human relations is important. [10] As an anthropology major at Michigan State University, you can choose to pursue either a bachelor of arts or bachelor of science degree. [8] Both programs provide a strong liberal arts education with exposure to all subfields of anthropology while permitting you sufficient freedom to pursue secondary areas of study. [8] For either degree, you complete the standard University requirements and College of Social Science requirements in addition to a minimum of 30 credits in Anthropology Coursework. [8] You begin by taking three introductory-level classes, one introduction to cultural anthropology, one introduction to archaeology, and one introduction to physical anthropology, and one methods course. [8] In addition, you must also take one culture-area course and one thematic or analytical course. [8] Four additional courses are electives, but three of them must be at the 300-level or above. [8] To complete the major, you must take the anthropology capstone course, which also satisfies the University's Tier II writing requirement. [8] In addition to required coursework, the undergraduate anthropology major allows you approximately 30 credits of elective coursework. [8] You can use these credits to pursue supplemental programs, such as an additional major in another department, a minor a second language, a thematic area, or a specialization. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Arabic
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Arabic is designed to develop both the linguistic and intercultural skills of students to an advanced level of language competency. Students will study modern standard Arabic and Arabic culture and literature. The major focuses on creating proficient speakers of Arabic who can apply their language skills in a variety of disciplines and careers.
ScholarshipType: Michigan State University offers a variety of scholarships, including merit-based scholarships which are considered based on academic achievement. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art Education
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Fine Arts degree program with a major in art education requires meeting the general admission requirements for Michigan State University. Specific requirements for the major are not detailed for initial application, but to be recommended for teacher certification later in the program, a student must meet several criteria. These include completing all teaching major and teacher certification coursework, maintaining a GPA of 2.5 or above overall and in the major, earning at least a 2.5 GPA in pre-internship professional education courses (with no grade below 2.0), and passing the Michigan Test for Teacher Certification. [19]
Description: Art Education at Michigan State University is an integrated, compound discipline that requires intensive training in studio art and art history, while also drawing resources from the social and cognitive sciences to explore contemporary issues in visual culture. The program is designed to develop specialized skills and conceptual content in studio art and art history, and includes pedagogy-specific content with pre-service and internship experiences in elementary and secondary school settings. Students in the Art Education curriculum study various approaches, including lessons that integrate art with other subjects, and those based in visual culture, social justice, and culturally responsive models. All coursework has an accompanying practicum for students to apply their knowledge in a field setting. The program follows the National Art Education Association Standards for Art Teacher Preparation.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History and Visual Culture
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive, but there are no minimum requirements. First-year admission is based on your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, and your ACT or SAT results. [6] MSU strongly encourages a college preparatory curriculum in high school. [6]
Description: Students of art history and visual culture investigate the production, form and reception of images and objects, past and present, from a multicultural perspective. This incorporates painting, sculpture and architecture as conventionally defined by art history but extends to material culture and a wide range of media. Art history and visual culture poses questions regarding the social, economic, religious, philosophical and psychological influences affecting those who consume as well as those who produce images and objects. Broadly speaking, this involves how values and beliefs are given material form and how these forms themselves can be interpreted.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Arts and Humanities
Requirements: Requirements for the Bachelor of Arts Degree in the Arts and Humanities include the completion of 120 credits, which encompasses the University's general requirements for bachelor's degrees. Specific to the college, students must complete 36 credits of RCAH courses, including core classes like Writing in Transcultural Contexts, Writing, Research, and Technologies, and an Introduction to the Arts and Humanities. The curriculum is structured around pathways in Arts, Community Engagement, Language and Culture, or Humanities. Additionally, there are language and culture requirements and a mandate for an experiential learning opportunity of at least 50 hours. [2, 3]
Department: Residential College in the Arts and Humanities
ScholarshipAmount: Awards of $1,000 and $2,000 are available.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Astrophysics and Astronomy
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Astrophysics is designed to provide an extensive background in both physics and astrophysics. A total of 120 credits are required for the degree. This includes fulfilling the University and College of Natural Science requirements, as well as completing the major's specific course requirements in mathematics, physics, and astronomy. The university's Tier II writing requirement is met by completing Astronomy and Astrophysics 410. [1]
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree with a major in Astrophysics is designed to provide an extensive background in both physics and astrophysics; a student who graduates with this degree may apply for admission to graduate study in either astronomy or physics. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Athletic Training
Requirements: Michigan State University no longer offers the Bachelor of Science in Athletic Training to new students. The program has transitioned to a Master of Science in Athletic Training (MSAT). [21] The final incoming class for the bachelor's program was in the Fall of 2017. [21] Consequently, application requirements for new students for the bachelor's program are no longer available.
Concentration: Kinesiology major with a concentration in athletic training

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Composition
Requirements: Applicants must submit two applications: the main university application and the College of Music Supplemental Application. [2] A portfolio containing three to five original compositions and/or musical arrangements is required. [2] At least two of these must be accurately notated, two must have recordings (performances or MIDI), and one must be at least five minutes long. [2] An informal interview with the composition faculty is also required and will be scheduled on the applicant's audition day. [2] Additionally, applicants must complete an audition on their primary instrument or voice. [2]
Description: The Bachelor of Music degree program in composition is designed for students who are interested in obtaining a strong foundation in music composition and for students who are preparing for advanced study in music composition, music theory, or musicology. [3]
Accredidation: All degree programs in the College of Music are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Education
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Music in Music Education program, applicants must first be admitted to Michigan State University. Following university admission, a secondary application to the College of Music is required. This supplemental application includes an audition and an interview. The purpose of the interview and an associated aural skills test is to provide the admissions committee with a more complete picture of the applicant's qualifications. Candidates will be asked about their musical background, academic record, teaching or leadership experiences, and their motivations for becoming a music teacher. The evaluation will be based on the applicant's background, interests and attitudes about teaching, and communication skills. For the aural skills test, applicants will be asked to echo simple melodic and rhythmic patterns and sing a short song of their choice. [10]
Description: An admissions audition is required for consideration.  University and Music Supplemental Application.  The College of Music Supplemental Application deadline is Dec 1 for Fall applicants, and Oct 1 for Spring applicants.  Current MSU students do not file a main university application. Instead, file only the Music Supplemental Application.  This interview will take place during your audition day. The purpose of the interview and aural skills test is to provide our admissions committee with a more complete picture of your qualifications as a music education student. During the interview, you will be asked questions about your musical background, your academic record, your teaching or leadership experiences, and your thoughts about becoming a music teacher. You will be evaluated on your background, your interests and attitudes about teaching, and your communication skills.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music Performance
Description: The Bachelor of Music in Performance is a professional program for students who demonstrate outstanding musical performance and wish to pursue a career as a performer and/or studio teacher. This degree also provides the necessary foundation for students who may wish to pursue graduate degrees in music. Students in this program receive a high level of training in their primary performance area, including lessons and coaching with world-class faculty. In addition, students gain a broad understanding of the historical and theoretical aspects of music, and develop as artists through a wide range of ensemble experiences.
Accredidation: The Michigan State University College of Music is a member of the National Association of Schools of Music. The courses of study for this degree are in conformity with the regulations and standards of the Association.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Requirements: Applicants are expected to have completed a rigorous college preparatory curriculum. This includes four years of English, three years of mathematics (including Algebra I, Geometry, and Algebra II), three years of social studies (including U.S. history), and three years of science. Two years of a single foreign language are also recommended. Admission is competitive, and decisions are based on a holistic review of the student's academic performance, the rigor of their curriculum, and their personal essay.
Description: The Bachelor of Science program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology for students in the College of Natural Science combines the elements of a liberal education with thorough preparation in biochemistry and molecular biology and the underlying principles of biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. [5] It is intended primarily for those students who wish to pursue a career in which a sound knowledge of biochemistry and molecular biology is necessary, or for students who plan further studies at the graduate or professional level. [5] With suitable choice of electives, the B.S. program offers the option of merging rigorous training in biochemistry and molecular biology with development of writing or pedagogical skills, leading to career options in science writing or teaching. [5] Undergraduate students are taught by professors who are familiar with the changing directions and emphases in the field of biochemistry and molecular biology. [5] Interested undergraduates are encouraged to participate, along with graduate students and postdoctoral fellows, in the on–going research of one of the faculty members. [5] Students seeking admission to the program should complete the high school science or college preparatory curriculum, ensuring that their programs include courses required for admission to the university. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry/Biotechnology
Requirements: Admission is based on a comprehensive review of academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of the curriculum, recent trends in academic performance, class rank, and standardized test results. Leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience are also considered.
Description: The Bachelor of Science program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology/Biotechnology is intended primarily for those students who plan to pursue careers in industry, veterinary medicine, or related health sciences, or for students who plan advanced study in biotechnology and molecular biology. [1] The core curriculum in the Biochemistry and Molecular Biology/Biotechnology program is identical to that of the Biochemistry and Molecular Biology program. [1] Additional course work introduces the student to the chemical engineering and microbiological aspects of biotechnology and allows for specialization through a broad range of approved biotechnology courses in the junior and senior years. [1, 4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Science-Secondary Education
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Biological Science-Secondary Education program is contingent upon admission to Michigan State University. The program is offered through the College of Natural Science and as a coordinate major in Lyman Briggs College. For first-year admissions into Lyman Briggs College, there are no additional academic or program requirements beyond those for general university admission. [95]
Description: The college offers interdepartmental majors: biological science–secondary education, human biology, and physical science-secondary education. The interdepartmental major features study in several disciplines with no single discipline being dominant and is generally considered the proper choice if breadth of background in several fields of the natural sciences is desired. [4]
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. Information about the accreditation of individual programs is included in program descriptions in the Academic Programs Catalog. [4] No program-specific accreditation is mentioned for the Bachelor of Science in Biological Science-Secondary Education on the pages that were reviewed.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering program is handled through admission to the College of Engineering. Admission is based on the cumulative grade-point average of all courses taken and a grade-point average calculated on mathematics, physical and biological sciences, and engineering courses. For specific course requirements for admission to the College of Engineering, students should contact the Undergraduate Studies office in the College of Engineering.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Laboratory Science
Requirements: Requirements for the Bachelor of Science Degree in Biomedical Laboratory Science include the completion of 120 credits. The University's Tier II writing requirement for the major is met by completing Biomedical Laboratory Diagnostics 456. [8] The program is designed to prepare students for careers in various fields such as the medical laboratory, public health, research, industry, and for further education in human medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, or graduate school. [8]
Description: the biomedical laboratory science (bls) academic program (major) is designed to prepare students for careers in a variety of applied biomedical sciences. these include careers in the medical laboratory, public health, research, industry, human medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, graduate school or other human health professional education. the bld courses are focused in curricular spirals within six disciplines: clinical chemistry, molecular diagnostics, immunology and immunohematology, hematology and hemostasis, medical microbiology and professional writing (with a research and laboratory medicine emphasis). the medical laboratory experience required for national certification as a medical laboratory scientist is not included in this program, though bls program advisors help students plan their career pathways. students desiring medical laboratory science certification are recommended to complete the medical laboratory science concentration and are responsible for securing accredited clinical experiences subsequent to completion of the degree. the biomedical laboratory diagnostics program will advise students in securing clinical practicum experiences. the program will also provide advising and career support for students pursuing career pathways in public health, research, industry, human medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, or graduate school. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biosystems Engineering
Requirements: Michigan State University's undergraduate application process is for all majors, and there are no specific prerequisite courses or a separate application required for admission to the Biosystems Engineering program. General admission requirements apply.
Concentration: ['Bioenergy and Bioproduct Engineering', 'Biomedical Engineering', 'Ecosystems Engineering', 'Food Engineering']
Description: Biosystems engineers design solutions to technical problems that involve a critical biological component. They apply quantitative skills to create products, processes, and systems that improve human existence. Working at the interface of engineering and biology, biosystems engineers are engaged in the most important challenges of our time. Biosystems engineers may, for example, design pathogen control processes to protect the safety of our food supply, constructed wetlands to improve water quality and quantity, biomass conversion processes to sustainably supply renewable energy and products, and/or diagnostic and risk modeling systems to protect and enhance human and animal health. Biosystems engineers are sought after by a wide variety of employers that need creative individuals to integrate principles of engineering and biology, including food manufacturers, environmental consulting firms, health industries, and government agencies.
Accredidation: The Biosystems Engineering (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the General Criteria and Program Criteria for Biological and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chinese
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Chinese is designed to equip students with functional proficiency in the language, and cultural sensitivity to and factual knowledge about China. [4] Study abroad is encouraged to provide students with firsthand experience of cultures superficially different from those to which they are accustomed, but are similar in many ways at the level of human interaction. [4] Students who plan to complete the requirements for the major should consult an undergraduate advisor in Chinese. [4]
ScholarshipType: Michigan State University offers a variety of scholarships, which can be broadly categorized as merit-based and need-based. [2, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Choral Music Education
Description: Michigan State University offers a Bachelor of Music in Music Education that provides comprehensive training for aspiring music teachers. The program is designed to allow students to tailor a course of study that aligns with their specific interests and career goals. Students are encouraged to develop their musicianship through participation in ensembles, private lessons, conducting classes, a creative musicianship component, and various instrumental and voice classes. The curriculum for educators begins in the freshman year and concludes with a full-time student teaching internship in an area school during the final semester. Graduates are equipped to plan, implement, and evaluate music instruction in diverse settings and for various student populations. This program leads to K-12 music teacher certification in Michigan. [12]
Accredidation: All of Michigan State University's music education programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Citizenship
Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Requirements: To be admitted to the university, students must submit an application. First-year admission is based on academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of the curriculum, recent academic performance trends, class rank, and leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [8] The university recommends a strong college preparatory curriculum including four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies, and two years each of science and a single foreign language. [8] For the Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering, a total of 128 credits are required. [13] The university's Tier II writing requirement for the major is met by completing Civil Engineering 321 and 341. [13]
Description: The civil engineering major is designed to provide graduates with a broad understanding of the physical factors involved in the planning, design, and operation of public and private facilities. The bachelor's degree program in civil engineering is oriented to the application of engineering principles to several areas of specialization, including transportation, structures, geotechnical engineering, environmental engineering, water resources, and pavements and materials. [8, 15]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science Degree program in Civil Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org. [8, 12, 15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical and Ancient Mediterranean Studies
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University for a bachelor's degree is based on a holistic review of several factors. These include your academic performance in high school, the rigor of your curriculum, recent academic trends, and class rank. [6, 9] An essay is a required part of the application. [7, 9] While MSU is test-optional, if you choose to submit ACT or SAT scores, they will be considered. [6, 9] The university also considers your leadership experience, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [6, 9] There are no specified minimum requirements to apply. [6, 9]
Description:
The Bachelor of Arts degree in Classical and Ancient Mediterranean Studies is an interdisciplinary program for students who want to study the history, literature, art, and archaeology of ancient Greece and Rome and their relationships with the cultures of the Near East and Egypt. 

The program is designed for students who are interested in a broad-ranging liberal arts education that focuses on the origins of Western and Mediterranean civilizations. The program also prepares students for graduate study in a variety of fields, including ancient history, archaeology, and classical studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience
Requirements: Michigan State University does not have a specific major called 'Bachelor of Science in Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience'. It offers a Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience with a concentration in 'Cognitive and Systems Neuroscience'. The general application requirements for undergraduate admission to Michigan State University apply. These include submission of an application, a personal statement, and an official high school transcript. The submission of a resume is optional.
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Neuroscience is for students who wish to pursue a career in which a broad-based knowledge of the structure and function of the nervous system is necessary, including careers in research, education, healthcare or business. It is also intended for those students who seek admission to graduate study in neuroscience or health-related professional schools.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication
Requirements: To apply for first-year admission, applicants must submit an application along with a fee (or an eligible fee waiver), have their official high school transcripts forwarded to the university, and write one essay from a selection of prompts. [7] Michigan State University recommends a high school curriculum that includes four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies, and two years each of science and a single foreign language. [10]
Department: College of Communication Arts and Sciences
Concentration: ['Intercultural Communication', 'Social Influence', 'Communication Science, Analytics, and Research Methods', 'Interpersonal Communication', 'Mediated Communication', 'Health Communication', 'Organizational Communication']
Description: The B.A. in Communication program prepares you for the workplace, whether that workplace is in a for-profit corporation, a nonprofit, a government agency or an entrepreneurial start-up. With a strong training in communication research and presentation, you'll use your skills of persuasion and leadership to influence society and make noticeable, positive changes in the world around you. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication
Department: College of Communication Arts and Sciences

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication Sciences and Disorders
Department: College of Communication Arts and Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Communicative Sciences and Disorders is a pre-professional degree for students who are preparing to pursue graduate study in speech-language pathology, audiology, or related disciplines. The program is designed to provide students with a strong foundational knowledge of basic communication processes and an introduction to communication disorders.
ScholarshipType: A variety of CSD scholarships and awards are available to students studying Communicative Sciences and Disorders. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Cultures and Politics
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Comparative Cultures and Politics, prospective students must complete the general Michigan State University undergraduate application and select James Madison College as their intended major. [1, 3] The application process is integrated with MSU's Office of Admissions. [1]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in comparative politics and culture focuses on the intersection of culture and politics in matters of global public affairs. An innovative interdisciplinary approach in the humanities and social sciences gives students the skills they need to address complex and critical global issues across academic and professional fields. The major gives students the tools to better understand diverse cultural perspectives around the world, how culture shapes power relations and how political and economic dynamics impact culture. The comparative and transnational focus encourages students to learn about other cultures and political systems, to reflect on their own societies and to discover how they want to position themselves as globally engaged citizens.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Composition
Requirements: An admissions audition and a portfolio of compositions is required for consideration. [2] Applicants must create two applications: the main university application and a Music Supplemental Application. [2] An informal interview with members of the composition faculty will also be scheduled. [2]
Description: The Bachelor of Music degree program in composition is designed for students who are interested in obtaining a strong foundation in music composition and for students who are preparing for advanced study in music composition, music theory, or musicology.
Accredidation: The Michigan State University College of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computational Data Science
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Computational Data Science focuses on the computational foundations of data science, providing an in-depth understanding of the algorithms and data structures for storing, manipulating, visualizing, and learning from large data sets. [3, 7, 8, 11] Students in the program have unique access to a wide range of fundamental computer science courses in topics ranging from mobile application and web development to theory of computation and fundamental algorithms. [3, 6, 11] Students can tailor their degree to their unique interests and requirements, with an emphasis on computational foundations. [3, 6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: General admission to Michigan State University for first-year students is based on a holistic review of academic performance in high school, the rigor and quality of the curriculum, recent academic trends, class rank, and a student's leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experiences. While there are no minimum requirements, a strong college preparatory curriculum is strongly encouraged.
Fees: For the 2023-2024 academic year, full-time (12-18 credits) undergraduate tuition for the College of Engineering was $9,043 per semester for Michigan residents (lower division) and $29,040 per semester for non-residents (lower division). Upper division rates were $1,337 per credit for residents and $3,079 per credit for non-residents. [12]
Description: The undergraduate program in computer engineering focuses on the theory, design, and applications of digital computers, principles of software design and integration of hardware with software. Computer engineering is concerned with the organization and design of computers and computer systems. The study of computer hardware and software, and their integration and application, is emphasized. [4]  It prepares its graduates for a variety of career paths including engineering positions directly after program completion, entry to engineering graduate school, and entry to other professional graduate-level schools, and eventual leadership in scientific, technical, academic, governmental, and entrepreneurial arenas. [3] The program is structured to establish analytical and design skills in areas such as computer architecture, digital logic design, analog and mixed-signal circuits, computer communication networks, digital computer control, integrated circuit engineering, software engineering, operating systems, data structures and algorithms, computer–aided engineering, and electronic design automation. [4] Complementing these fundamentals, the program also provides opportunities for specialization in individually selected areas of interest. [4]
Accredidation: The Computer Engineering (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the General Criteria and Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [3]
AverageScholarshipAmount: The College of Engineering offers over 150 scholarships totaling approximately $300,000 annually to incoming students, making the average award around $2,000. [27]
CostPerCredit: For the 2023-2024 academic year, the per-credit cost for lower division (0-54 credits) undergraduate courses in the College of Engineering was $1,116 for Michigan residents and $2,782 for non-residents. For upper division (55+ credits) courses, the cost was $1,337 per credit for residents and $3,079 for non-residents. [12]
ScholarshipAmount: Individual scholarships for incoming first-year students in the College of Engineering typically range from $1,000 to $8,500. [27]
ScholarshipType: Scholarships are primarily awarded based on academic excellence, with financial need also being a consideration for some awards. [27]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
Requirements: To be admitted, students must be admissible to the university. For additional information, refer to the university's admission requirements for first-year students.
Description: The   Department of Computer Science and Engineering   offers undergraduate programs in both computer science and computer engineering. A student in computer science is interested in the analysis, design, and development of software and hardware computer systems. A computer engineering student has a special interest in the design and application of computer systems, including embedded computer systems. The cognate provides an excellent opportunity to complement the major areas with an individually selected area of interest.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree program in Computer Science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
MinGPA: Students must have a minimum grade of 2.0 in each of the following courses: CSE 300, CSE 320, CSE 325, CSE 331, CSE 335, CSE 380. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Construction Management
Department: School of Planning, Design, and Construction
Description: The construction management major provides students with a background in project management, technological building practices, and the economic, social, political and environmental aspects of residential and commercial construction. Students take classes in contracts, finance, estimating, scheduling, project management, real estate, structural design, accounting, building codes, business law, safety and materials. They are provided opportunities to receive real-world experiences through a well-established internship program.
Accredidation: The Construction Management major is nationally accredited by the American Council for Construction Education since 1999. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Creative Writing
Description: The creative writing concentration at MSU offers students a program that blends foundational work in literary studies, exploration of create-writing in multiple genres, and a focused capstone experience. Students graduate with a B.A. in English, but their diplomas note their dedicated commitment to creative writing. Beginning with the same foundation as other English majors, students also work at the introductory and advanced level in at least two different genres of creative writing. Many then choose to write a senior thesis in a single genre, creating in the last year of study a collection of poems or stories, a novel, or a finished screenplay; students might also pursue internships in writing and editing. Our program provides many co-curricular events and opportunities, including a reading series, writing workshops, brown bag lunch conversations with faculty and visiting writers. The Michigan State University English Department is also home to Red Cedar Review, one of the oldest student-managed literary journals in the United States.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree program in criminal justice is designed to prepare students for entry level positions in public and private agencies identified with criminal justice administration. [9, 10] Such agencies apprehend offenders, adjudicate alleged offenses, redirect emergent criminal careers, and promote industrial and commercial security. [9, 10] Such agencies also encourage and emphasize community responsibility for the success of their programs. The bachelor's program in criminal justice provides a basic orientation to the institutions and processes of criminal justice and offers students wide exposure to all of the major disciplines of the criminal justice system. [9, 10] The program promotes general knowledge through core and social science courses. It provides students with the opportunity to pursue interests in the following areas: juvenile justice, police administration, adult corrections, and security. [9, 10]
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [4, 12] Information about the accreditation of individual programs is included in program descriptions in the Academic Programs Catalog. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Crop and Soil Sciences
Department: College of Agriculture & Natural Resources, Department of Plant, Soil and Microbial Sciences
Description: The Crop and Soil Sciences major is based upon the an ever-expanding knowledge base of the biological and physical sciences and the use of those sciences to produce high-quality food and fiber on a competitive basis to promote sustainability, and to obtain increased nutrient–use efficiency, proper land use, increased plant adaptation to environmental and other stresses, decreased soil erosion, and decreased environmental pollution. [4] Crop and soil scientists use the principles of genetics, plant breeding, crop physiology, weed science, turfgrass science, soil physics, soil fertility, soil genesis and classification, and soil chemistry. [4] Majors complete a common core of courses and one of three concentrations: Agronomic Sciences, Turfgrass Management, or Advanced Study. [4]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships are available from the Department of Plant, Soil and Microbial Sciences based on GPA. The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources also offers scholarships. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Science
Requirements: The application requirements are the general freshman admission requirements for Michigan State University. For graduation, students must complete 120 credits, including university general education requirements and the specific course curriculum for the major from the College of Engineering and College of Natural Science. [34]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Dietetics
Description: The dietetics program focuses on the study of food and nutrition in relation to preventing and treating disease and maintaining and promoting good health. Dietetics is a people-oriented, science-focused and evidence-based field. Studying dietetics is the first step toward earning the registered dietitian professional credential.
Accredidation: The MSU Dietetics undergraduate program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) as a didactic program in dietetics (DPD) that meets or exceeds the minimum academic requirements for professionally qualified dietitians.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Digital Storytelling
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Digital Storytelling program falls under the general undergraduate admission requirements for Michigan State University. There are no specific, separate application requirements mentioned for this program on the official MSU websites. The university reviews freshman applications based on high school coursework, grades, and a personal statement. Standardized test scores (ACT/SAT) are optional.
Department: College of Communication Arts and Sciences
Description: Digital storytelling is the foundation for the world of media. The Bachelor of Arts degree in Digital Storytelling prepares students for a career in a media-focused world and provides them with the tools and techniques needed for creative, entrepreneurial and analytical processes and production. Graduates are prepared for a multitude of career paths -- film, television, corporate communications, digital advertising, new media—anything that involves using sound and image to entertain, inform and/or educate. [6] The digital storytelling major has an interdisciplinary focus with courses from Communication Arts and Science, Film Studies, and Journalism. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Earth Science-Secondary Education
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Geological Sciences provides students with a broad background in the fundamentals of the geological sciences and the supporting sciences of chemistry, physics, and mathematics. The flexibility of this degree program makes it an ideal choice for students who have a broad interest in the geological sciences, who wish to pursue a double major, who wish to prepare for a career in K-12 education, or who wish to pursue a career in environmental law or public policy.
Accredidation: The Michigan State University College of Education Educator Preparation Programs are accredited under the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) standards. [44] The current accreditation approval is from May 2022 to June 2029. [44]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Economics
Requirements: General application requirements for freshman admission to Michigan State University apply. These include a review of the high school transcript, GPA, and personal essays. MSU practices a holistic review of applications.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts Degree in Economics emphasizes the use of quantitative techniques in the analysis of economic theories. As an economics major, you will receive an extensive education in domestic and international economy. You will also study economic institutions, concepts and policy, as well as the tools of economic analysis. If you're more interested in theory and practical application of economics, the B.A. is a good fit for you. (If you're more interested in the math, statistics and computer science components of economics, view our B.S. in economics information to see if that might be a better fit.) An economics major will prepare you careers in business, such as in banking, financial markets, insurance, law, management and consulting; in national, state and local governments; and in teaching, and for graduate study in economics and related fields, including business administration, finance, public policy, and law.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Economics
Description: The Bachelor of Science Degree in Economics emphasizes the use of advanced math and science in the analysis of economic theories. The program offers students more emphasis on mathematics, statistics, and computer science, as preparation for those who wish to pursue graduate training in economics.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive, but there are no minimum requirements. First-year admission is based on: your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, your ACT or SAT results (MSU is test optional), and your leadership, talents, conduct and diversity of experience. [29] MSU recommends a strong college preparatory curriculum that includes: Four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies, two years of science, and two years of a single foreign language. [29] The university requirements for the Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering are 128 credits. [10]
Description: The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers a program leading to the Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering. Electrical engineers created the technology of the 21st century, from the electric power that lights the world, to the computers and communication systems that have wired it. Electrical engineering is the largest and most diverse of all engineering fields. The undergraduate program provides students a foundation of knowledge in the areas of digital systems, electronics, and physical systems (electromagnetics). An electrical engineering degree can lead to a career in a wide range of fields, including aerospace, communications, computers, and consumer electronics.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree program in Electrical Engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Elementary Education
Requirements: For first-year admission, applicants must submit an application and an essay (minimum 250 words, maximum 650 words). [11] A high school diploma or equivalent is required, along with official transcripts from all high schools attended. [6] Admission is competitive and based on a holistic review of factors including: academic performance in high school, strength of curriculum, recent academic trends, class rank, leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [12] Submission of ACT or SAT scores is optional. [12] There are no minimum requirements for admission. [12]
Description: The Elementary Teacher Preparation Program at Michigan State University is a four-year program with an emphasis on preparing professional elementary teachers. We have been ranked No. 1 in the nation for elementary (and secondary) education for three consecutive decades (U.S. News & World Report). The No. 1 ranking reflects our commitment to developing and mentoring excellent teaching practices. It also reflects our outstanding reputation with superintendents, principals, teachers and educators not only in Michigan, but around the globe. The reason for this reputation is a simple one: a high-quality education from a world-class university. You’ll learn from leading faculty who are experts in their field. The reason for this reputation araştırması is simple: MSU's College of Education develops teacher leaders. You will gain knowledge and skills to teach all subjects in pre-kindergarten through third grade (PK-3) or third grade through sixth grade (3-6) and in an additional endorsement area (ESL or Birth-K). Key elements of the program include a strong foundation in all content areas plus additional depth in your endorsement area, courses on the most effective teaching practices with a focus on supporting equity and social justice, and a full-year, guided teaching internship in a public school after completing the bachelor's degree.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in English
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is based on a holistic review of various factors. These include your academic performance in high school, the rigor of your curriculum, recent academic trends, and your class rank. Additionally, leadership qualities, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience are considered. Applicants must have a high school diploma or its equivalent and submit an essay. Official transcripts from all high schools attended are also required.
Description: An English major at Michigan State University offers a dynamic blend of creative inquiry and analytical thought. Students can opt for a broad-based literary studies track, or choose to specialize in creative writing, popular culture, or prepare for a career in secondary English education. The program emphasizes close student-faculty interaction within a collaborative setting, fostering the essential skills for success across a wide array of professions. The curriculum is designed to equip students with the ability to identify, evaluate, and navigate the complex challenges found in all social and professional environments. Graduates develop strong critical thinking and writing abilities, as well as the creativity and problem-solving skills needed in a constantly evolving world.
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [14] Information regarding the accreditation of individual programs is available in the Academic Programs Catalog. [14]
ScholarshipAmount: Awards may range from $500 to $5,000. [8]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships such as the College of Arts & Letters Outstanding Senior Achievement Award and the Alumni Award for Undergraduate Excellence. [8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Entomology
Requirements: General application requirements for freshman admission to Michigan State University include submitting an application, paying the application fee, and providing an official high school transcript. The university also evaluates students based on their high school curriculum, academic performance, and class rank.
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources
Concentration: While no specific concentrations are listed on the main program page, students can complete the major through Lyman Briggs College (LBC), which is a residential college at MSU focused on science-focused academics with a small-community experience. [8]
Description: The undergraduate program in Entomology leads to the Bachelor of Science degree. Courses are designed to give the student an understanding of the structure, classification, identification, function, biology, ecology, and management of beneficial and harmful arthropods, and the communities and ecosystems where insects occur. [4] At MSU, an entomology degree gives you a broad foundation in the biological sciences, using insects as a window into the complexity of life. You'll explore relationships across ecosystems and build skills that apply to ecology, conservation, pest management and beyond. [8] The program provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the biology, ecology, evolution, identification, structure, classification and management of beneficial and harmful insects. Core areas of study include organismal and molecular biology, ecology, plant biology and pathology, chemistry, physics, soil science, and pest management. [3] Opportunities are available for undergraduate students to carry out research projects, gain work experience, and participate in internships and study abroad programs. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Biology/Microbiology
Description: Many of the environmental problems facing society are microbiological ones, or ones for which microbiological solutions may be found. The Bachelor of Science degree program with a major in environmental biology/microbiology is designed for students who plan to pursue careers involving microbiology and the environment or who plan to pursue graduate study in microbiology and related environmental areas. The educational objectives of the program are to: Help students to acquire knowledge of microbiology and related environmental areas. Prepare students to solve problems in environmental microbiology. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Biology/Plant Biology
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree program in environmental biology/plant biology is designed for students who plan to pursue careers involving plants and the environment or who plan to pursue graduate study in the biological sciences. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Biology/Zoology
Requirements: The admissions office at Michigan State University uses a holistic review process that primarily considers your academic record, including rigorous course selection, grade trends, and cumulative unweighted GPA. [3] Secondary factors include how you spend your time outside the classroom, explanations for any time away from school, and reflections on your personal strengths and experiences. [3]
Description: The objective of the Bachelor of Science degree program with a major in environmental biology/zoology is to help students to understand the concepts of environmental biology and to apply those concepts to improve both the natural environment and the environment perturbed by human activities. The focus of the program is on animal biology. The integrative biology courses in the program emphasize ecology, systematics, and environmental science.
ScholarshipType: The College of Natural Science offers various scholarships, some based on financial need, Michigan residency, or graduating from specific high schools. [48] There are also scholarships for juniors and seniors with a certain GPA, and for those pursuing teaching. [48] Additionally, undergraduate research scholarships are available. [59]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Economics and Management
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources
Description: Environmental Economics and Management prepares students for careers that require consideration of environmental sustainability and economic performance goals for the public sector and businesses. [4] The business component has a particular focus on resource, agricultural, and food industries, as these have strong environmental linkages. [4] The major develops skills in environmental economics and policy analysis as well as core business disciplines such as accounting, marketing, and supply chain management. [4] Business skills and knowledge are developed to help manage or create environmentally and socially responsive business organizations that also deliver shareholder value. [4] The major is a broad, integrated study of environmental economics, public finance, economic development, community and regional studies and environmental science. [3] The major prepares students for sustainability related employment opportunities with state and federal government agencies, non-profit organizations, the agricultural and food industry, and consulting firms. [4] It also offers students the opportunity to prepare for graduate study in environmental economics and policy or business programs. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering
Requirements: Applicants are expected to have a strong college preparatory curriculum. While Michigan State University does not have a specific set of required high school courses, a rigorous curriculum that includes English, mathematics, social studies, science, and foreign language is recommended.
