The university practices a holistic review of applications, considering academic performance, the rigor of the curriculum, and an optional personal essay.
Description: Environmental engineers are involved in the application of scientific and engineering principles to assess, manage and design sustainable environmental systems for the protection of human and ecological health. Graduates research, plan, design, and/or perform engineering duties in the prevention, control, and remediation of environmental hazards related to water and wastewater treatment, hazardous waste treatment, storm water management, site remediation, or air pollution monitoring and control.
Accredidation: The Environmental Engineering (B.S.) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Environmental and Similarly Named Engineering Programs. [14]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Geosciences
Requirements: Admission to the university is based on a holistic review of the applicant's academic record, including the rigor of the curriculum, grades, and any available standardized test scores. While not explicitly stated for this specific program, general undergraduate admission to Michigan State University does not require a resume, statement of purpose, or writing sample for most programs. For detailed admission criteria, it is recommended to consult the university's official admissions website.
Description: The Major in Environmental Geosciences provides interdisciplinary training for students interested in the environmental sciences including opportunities to study in field, laboratory, and computational environments. [3] The Major is available to students enrolled at Michigan State University within the College of Natural Sciences, and it is administered by the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences. [3]
ScholarshipType: Departmental Undergraduate Scholarships are available to all majors in our Earth Sciences and Environmental Geosciences programs. [23]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Science and Management
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive, but there are no minimum requirements. Freshman admission is based on your academic performance in high school; the strength and quality of your curriculum; recent trends in your academic performance; your class rank; your ACT or SAT results (if applicable, since MSU is test optional); and your leadership, talents, conduct and diversity of experience. [8] Typically, the most important element in the admissions process is high school academic achievement. [8] The university requires students to have a high school diploma or equivalent and to submit an essay with their application. [8]
Description: Listed below are the approved requirements for the program from the official Academic Programs Catalog. Students must consult their advisors to learn which specific requirements apply to their degree programs. A minimum of 41 credits from the courses listed below including: One of the following groups of courses (8 or 10 credits): LB 118, and STT 231 or MTH 132, MTH 133, and STT 231. One course from each of the following 7 areas (24 to 26 credits): Ecology, Geology, Taxonomy or Phylogenetic Biology, Biochemistry, Aquatic Systems, Microbiology, and EC 201. One course from each of the following three groups (9 to 11 credits): FOR 464 or SOC 452; FW 424 or FW 444; FW 410 or FW 417. [6]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Studies and Sustainability
Requirements: A total of 120 credits are required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Studies and Sustainability. The university's Tier II writing requirement for this major is met by completing Community Sustainability 300 or 310. Students may complete an alternative track to Integrative Studies in Biological and Physical Sciences that consists of Biological Science 162 and 172, and Chemistry 141. [1]
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Studies and Sustainability is available for students who are interested in the human dimensions of environmental and coupled human-natural systems. The major is administered by the Department of Community Sustainability in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources. The Environmental Studies and Sustainability major is designed to provide students with a broad-based, interdisciplinary, and holistic understanding of the relationship between humans and the natural environment from a social science perspective, and how that understanding can be used to inform and guide more sustainable individual and institutional behavior and decision-making.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Experience Architecture
Requirements: Michigan State University will not require a standardized test score (ACT or SAT) from domestic or international undergraduate applicants for admission. The university will use a holistic, test-optional review process. There is no specific mention of additional application requirements for the Bachelor of Arts in Experience Architecture program on the official Michigan State University website.
Description: TThe Bachelor of Arts degree in Experience Architecture (XA) is a cutting-edge, interdisciplinary major in the College of Arts & Letters at Michigan State University. Students studying XA are forward-thinkers and are interested in gaining advanced skills in architecting or designing experiences for people in digital and physical environments. Our program gives students exposure to aspects of maneuvering and creating web sites or apps such as designing, coding, writing and digital rhetoric. Due to this well-rounded nature of the major, XA students are prepared for a number of careers or graduate programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Film and Media Studies
Requirements:
The Film and Media Studies major is a limited-enrollment program.
To be considered for admission to the major, students must:
1. complete FMS 200 with a minimum grade of 2.0.
2. have a minimum 2.0 overall grade-point average.
Students who meet these requirements will be admitted.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Film Studies offers students in-depth education in the disciplinary understanding of film as a medium and in the critical analysis of films as interpretable texts. Students will gain an understanding of aspects of cinematic aesthetics, film grammar, the history of film, cultural contexts of film, and theoretical and critical approaches in film studies. [15] Our curriculum engages students in the history, theory, and production of world cinema. Classes examine cinema globally across a range of industrial and artisanal contexts, and encourage students to understand cinema as an art, business, and technology. [14, 15] Learning the craft of filmmaking as well as criticism, students develop the creative and critical skills necessary today in all areas of the creative arts. [14, 15] With this training, our graduates have gone on to a wide range of careers that utilize and depend on the moving image: from film production, digital distribution, and film criticism, to arts management, educational programming, and public affairs work. [14, 15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Finance
Requirements: To be admitted to the Finance major, students must meet the admission requirements for the Eli Broad College of Business. The university's Tier II writing requirement for the Finance major is met by completing Finance 414. A minimum grade-point average of 2.0 is required in the major field of concentration courses. [11, 13]
Description: The undergraduate program in finance provides students with the foundation for careers in corporate finance, investments, and financial institutions. The program focuses on the role of finance in supporting the functional areas of the business and the role of the financial system in the economy. Students develop analytical skills with a focus on financial decision making. The program offers an opportunity for students to gain in-depth knowledge of one or more of the specialty areas in finance such as investment analysis, portfolio management, corporate finance, financial institutions, or financial markets. Students who complete the Bachelor of Arts degree in Finance may be eligible for a variety of positions in financial institutions such as banks, insurance companies, and brokerage firms. They may also find opportunities in corporate finance departments of non-financial corporations, and in public and not-for-profit sectors of the economy.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Fisheries and Wildlife
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Fisheries and Wildlife program is based on the general admission requirements for first-year students at Michigan State University. These include academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of the curriculum, recent academic trends, and class rank. [4] MSU requires applicants to have completed four years of English, three years of mathematics (two years of algebra, one of geometry), three years of social studies, and two years of science. [4] Additionally, two years of a single foreign language are recommended. [4] An essay is also a required part of the undergraduate application. [7] The program itself includes coursework in life sciences, social sciences, and various techniques, along with an experiential learning component like an internship or study abroad. [8]
Concentration: ['Conservation Biology', 'Fisheries Biology and Management', 'Wildlife Biology and Management', 'Water Sciences', 'Fish and Wildlife Disease Ecology and Management', 'Pre-veterinary']
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Fisheries and Wildlife undergraduate major focuses on interactions between humans and the natural world. [1] The program of study includes course work in the life sciences, social sciences, and field, lab and analytic techniques; it also includes an experiential learning component, such as study abroad and/or professional internships. [1] This program prepares students with interests in the life sciences, social sciences, and environmental policy for rewarding careers in fisheries, wildlife, or water quality management, conservation biology, animal health, and applied ecology. [1] Our graduates most typically find employment with state and federal natural resource agencies, non-profit environmental organizations, private companies and consulting firms, as well as universities and colleges. [1]
ScholarshipType: The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources offers a variety of scholarships, and students can apply for multiple opportunities through a single application. [2]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food Science
Requirements: Admission to the university is the first step. For the Bachelor of Science degree in Food Science, a total of 120 credits are required for graduation. [4, 17] These credits are fulfilled by completing university, college, and major-specific requirements. [17] The university requirements for a bachelor's degree are outlined in the Undergraduate Education section of the catalog. [4] The university's Tier II writing requirement for the Food Science major is met by completing Food Science 402, 440, 441, 455, and 470. [4]
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources
Concentration: ['Basic Food Science', 'Food Business and Industry', 'Food Packaging', 'Food Technology']
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in food science is a multidisciplinary program that applies chemistry, microbiology, engineering and nutrition to develop new food products and processes to improve the safety and quality of food. The required courses stress the principles of food safety and preservation and the application of scientific principles to control and enhance the flavor, color, texture, and nutritive value of foods. Graduates may be employed by food and allied industries, federal and state governments, and sectors throughout academia to work at the interface between the production and delivery of food. The program also prepares students for advanced study in graduate and professional schools. [6, 10]
Accredidation: The major and concentrations are Approved by the Institute of Food Technologists Higher Education Review Board. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Forestry
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is based on a holistic review of the applicant. This includes academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of the curriculum, recent trends in academic performance, class rank, and leadership, talents, conduct and diversity of experience. There are no minimum requirements for admission.
Description: Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Science Degree in Forestry program develop an in-depth understanding of the natural and social sciences in order to manage forest ecosystems. [3] The Bachelor of Science degree is accredited by the Society of American Foresters. [3] Through hands-on laboratory experiences and field studies, students learn how to manage forests for a wide range of goals and acquire the skills to evaluate and ensure the ecological, economic, and social sustainability of forests. [3] They place emphasis on development of analytical and communications skills necessary to create a positive exchange of ideas between forestry professionals and non-technical audiences. [3] Students who graduate from this program will possess the professional training to enable them to contribute significantly to resolution of forest-centered environmental and resource problems. [3]
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree is accredited by the Society of American Foresters. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in French
Requirements: While the website for the Bachelor of Arts in French details the course and credit requirements for completing the degree, it does not specify any application requirements separate from the general university admission process. Applicants are expected to follow the standard first-year application procedures for Michigan State University.
Description: Designed for students who wish to develop excellent reading, writing, listening and speaking skills in the French language, the French and Francophone Studies major also allows students to build a strong understanding of the history and culture of French communities throughout the world. [12]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Games and Interactive Media
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Games and Interactive Media is available for students who are admitted to the major. The requirements for the degree are the University’s All-University requirements for bachelor’s degrees and the following major requirements.
Description: The Games and Interactive Media major will provide a depth of knowledge, and a uniform core with foundational knowledge in several areas related to games and interactivity, including: knowledge of the art, design and programming fundamentals of digital game development, as well as the history, social impacts, and business of games. [1] Students also gain valuable skills in communicating and collaborating in team-based projects while building a strong portfolio of games. [1] We partner with game studios to provide an authentic, real-world experience in our coursework. [1] Learning is project-based, resulting in a portfolio of small and large projects that reflects a broad variety of work. [1] Our students consistently produce high quality content and work for some of the largest and most respected game companies in the world (EA, Activision, Ubisoft, Rockstar, Blizzard, Bungie, Insomniac, and more). [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in General Management
Description: This major is only available to students admitted to the Broad College prior to fall 2015 as general management majors. [8] Students admitted beginning fall 2015 or those admitted prior to fall 2015 who want to change their major must adhere to the management major requirements. [8]
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [13] The Eli Broad College of Business, which houses the management program, has been accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) since 1953. [12]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in General Music
Requirements: First-year admission to Michigan State University is based on your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, and your leadership, talents, conduct and diversity of experience. [4] For the Bachelor of Arts in Music, applicants must submit both the main university application and the College of Music Supplemental Application. [4] The supplemental application requires a personal statement of 300-500 words describing your educational and musical background, goals, and career plans, as well as two letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your musical abilities. [4] A successful admissions audition is also required for the major. [4]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree program with a major in music is a liberal arts program with a strong emphasis in music. It may fulfill the requirements for entrance into a Master of Music program; it does not provide preparation for teacher certification in music. [5, 6, 7, 13]
Accredidation: All degree programs in the College of Music are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music. [5, 15]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Genomics and Molecular Genetics
Requirements: The University requirements for bachelor's degrees as described in the Undergraduate Education section of this catalog; 120 credits, including general elective credits, are required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Genetics and Genomics. The University's Tier II writing requirement for the Genetics and Genomics major is met by completing Microbiology, Genetics, and Immunology 434 or 494L. [10]
Description: The objective of the Bachelor of Science degree program with a major in genetics and genomics is to provide a broad foundation in science, with emphasis in genetics and genomics. [7] Although the majority of the course work is prescribed, students have an opportunity to tailor their degree program to their own interests within the field by choosing a suitable course combination from a slate of options. [7] In addition to the general degree requirements of the College of Natural Science, the undergraduate program in genetics and genomics encompasses fundamental training in chemistry, mathematics, physics, and biology. [7] This foundation provides the prerequisites for undertaking the basic courses in genetics and genomics. [7] In order to increase the flexibility of the program, and to provide additional intellectual stimulation, students are encouraged to participate in mentored independent research for at least two, and ideally three or more, semesters. [7] Independent research is available to both Honors College and other students, and often culminates with a report written in manuscript style or a presentation or seminar by the student. [7] This research may fulfill part of the department's capstone course requirement for the bachelor's degree with a major in genetics and genomics. [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geographic Information Science
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is based on a holistic review of your application. Factors considered include academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in academic performance, class rank, and your leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [4] An application essay with a minimum of 250 words and a maximum of 650 words is required. [8] MSU recommends a strong college preparatory curriculum, including: four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies, two years of science, and two years of a single foreign language. [4]
Department: Department of Geography, Environment, and Spatial Sciences
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Geography provides comprehensive academic training in the human dimensions of the environment, particularly how people are affected by the environment, and how they alter and change it. [15] Geographers describe, analyze, and explain the arrangement of the Earth's physical and social features. With training in both the natural and social sciences, geographers have a wide range of career opportunities in public, private, academic, and non-profit sectors. [15] The department has an emphasis on geospatial techniques such as GIS, remote sensing, drones, and data analytics. [3] The B.S. program offers specialized concentrations, including Earth Observation & Geospatial Analytics. [3]
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [5] The official program description in the academic catalog does not mention a separate accreditation for the Bachelor of Science in Geography program. [5, 15]
AverageScholarshipAmount: In 2024-25, the average aid (grants, scholarships) for in-state first-year students was $8,268 and $15,548 for out-of-state first-year students. [22]
CostPerCredit: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the resident undergraduate per-credit tuition rate (for 1-11 credits) is $563.75 for freshmen and $642.75 for juniors/seniors. [8]
ScholarshipAmount: Scholarship amounts for international students can be $18,000, $21,000, or $25,000 per year. [27]
ScholarshipType: Merit-based scholarships are available and considered automatically with the application for admission. [3] Departmental scholarships are also available. [10]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geography
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive, but there are no minimum requirements for the university. [3, 9] The Bachelor of Science in Geography program does not have separate admission requirements beyond being admitted to the university. First-year admission to the university is based on academic performance in high school, the strength of the curriculum, recent academic trends, and leadership and talents. [3, 9]
Concentration: ['Earth Observation and Geospatial Analytics', 'Human, Environment, and Economic Geography', 'Physical Environment and Climate']
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Geography provides comprehensive academictraining in the human dimensions of the environment, particularly howpeople are affected by the environment, and how they alter and change it.Geographic knowledge is essential for understanding rapid social andenvironmental change in a globalized society. Geographers describe,analyze, and explain the arrangement of the Earth's physical and socialfeatures. With training in both the natural and social sciences, geographershave a wide range of career opportunities in public, private, academic, andnon-profit sectors. Geographers are increasingly in demand for jobs thatrequire expertise in geospatial techniques, such as geographic informationsystems (GIS), global positioning systems (GPS), remote sensing,cartography, data science, and data analytics.
Accredidation: Information about the accreditation of individual programs, schools, and colleges is included in program descriptions in the Academic Programs catalog. [13] Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [13]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geological Sciences
Requirements: Michigan State University reviews freshman applications holistically. The primary factors for admission include academic performance in high school, with an emphasis on rigorous course selection (such as AP, IB, and dual enrollment), grade trends, and cumulative unweighted GPA. Secondary factors that are considered include personal statements and essays that provide insight into a student's experiences, talents, and strengths. Standardized test scores are generally not required but can be submitted as supplementary information.
Description: The Major in Geological Sciences provides interdisciplinary training for students interested in the solid Earth sciences including opportunities to study in field, laboratory, and computational environments. [3] The Major is available to students enrolled at Michigan State University within the College of Natural Sciences, and it is administered by the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences. [3] Students who plan to complete the requirements for the major should consult the undergraduate advisor in the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in German
Requirements: To earn a Bachelor of Arts degree in German, students must complete 120 credits. The major itself requires 34 to 40 credits of specific German (GRM) coursework. Requirements include: completing two courses from a set of 300-level options (like GRM 301, 302, 303, 304, or 311), taking six additional credits at the 300-level (including at least one literature/culture course), completing twelve credits at the 400-level, and a 1-credit capstone project (GRM 492). [11] Students with a primary major in German are also expected to participate in an approved education abroad experience. [11] The university's Tier II writing requirement is fulfilled by completing specific 400-level German courses. [11]
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in German provides for the study of the language, literature, and culture of Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. It is designed to provide students with a command of the language and a familiarity with the literatures and cultures of the German-speaking countries. The program offers a range of courses in language, linguistics, literature, and culture, from the beginning to the advanced level. Students are encouraged to spend a semester or a year in a German-speaking country as part of their program of study.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Global and International Studies
Requirements: For first-year applicants, a personal essay is a required part of the application. The essay should be between 250 and 650 words. [22] For graduate applicants, a personal or academic statement is typically required. [32] The specific requirements for the statement of purpose, including length and content, can vary by program.
Concentration: ['Asian Studies', 'Canadian Studies', 'European and Eurasian Studies', 'Latin American and Caribbean Studies', 'Middle East and African Studies', 'Global Health', 'International Development', 'Migration Studies', 'Integrative Studies']
Description: The Global and International Studies in Social Science major provides students with breadth in social science foundational courses combined with in-depth knowledge in a world region or global topic. World region concentrations include Asian Studies, Canadian Studies, European and Eurasian Studies, Latin American and Caribbean Studies, and Middle East and African Studies. Global topical concentrations include Global Health, International Development, and Migration Studies. Students can also work with faculty and advisors to design and complete an Integrative Studies concentration focused on a global topic of interest. Students enrolled in a concentration cannot complete a minor in the same concentration area. In addition to academic focus on a region or theme, students must demonstrate second-year foreign language competency in a non-English language relevant to their course of study. Students also engage in interdisciplinary thinking and research through required introductory, methods, and capstone courses.. Students are a strongly encouraged to have at least one international experience through study abroad, internships, or independent study. The major helps prepare students for jobs in government, business, and non-governmental organizations and for graduate study in international or area studies and other fields. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Graphic Design
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Graphic Design is a secondary step that occurs after a student has already been admitted to Michigan State University. To be accepted into the major, current MSU students must complete specific studio art and graphic design courses (GD 360 and GD 365) and then submit an application that includes a portfolio of their work. An oral interview may also be requested. This process typically occurs during the spring semester.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree in Graphic Design is a liberal arts-focused degree that provides students with a foundational understanding of the field, including design thinking, craft, and professional practices. The curriculum emphasizes the development of unique and effective visual communication through a combination of required and elective courses in graphic design, as well as studio art, art history, and other disciplines. The program prepares students for a variety of careers in the creative industries or for continued study in a graduate program.
ScholarshipAmount: Awards may range from $500 to $5,000 depending on available funds and the number of applicants. [5]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Greek
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree program in Greek is designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the language, literature, and culture of ancient Greece. Students develop a high level of proficiency in the ancient Greek language and a critical understanding of its most important literary works in their cultural and historical contexts. The study of Greek provides an excellent foundation for a number of professions such as law, medicine, and theology as well as for graduate study in classics, and a number of related disciplines such as ancient history, philosophy, and religious studies.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History
Requirements: First-year admission is based on your academic performance in high school; the strength and quality of your curriculum; recent trends in your academic performance; your class rank; your ACT or SAT results — however, please note that MSU is test optional and prospective students have the option to apply to MSU without submitting an ACT or SAT score; your leadership, talents, conduct and diversity of experience. [4, 11] MSU strongly encourages a college preparatory curriculum in high school which includes: four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies (including history), two years of science, and two years of a single foreign language. [4]
Description: A degree in History is one of the most flexible and rewarding you can get. [9] The History major is a rigorous Bachelor of Arts degree program that develops its students' ability to understand human societies—both past and present—in context, with a social science emphasis on applying knowledge of the past to the resolution of enduring social, political, and economic challenges. [9] The major is structured to develop student skills in research, writing, digital methods, and oral communication across the curriculum. [9] Students learn how gather and critically evaluate evidence from multiple types of sources, to conduct extensive archival or digital research, to build strong foundation in historical knowledge, gain expertise in analyzing social, political, and economic dynamics in different societies over space and time, apply understandings of different cultures to explain historical conflict and resolution, understand how power is expressed and challenged in within and between nations, and incorporate diverse viewpoints to analyze historical change. [9] The Department of History's research strengths allow students to focus on a range of geographic or thematic areas of study. [9] Geographic areas include the U.S., Europe, Africa, Asia, Latin America, or the globe. Thematic areas include race, ethnicity, politics, religion, gender and sexuality. By involving all students in the process of careful analysis of evidence and thoughtful, cogent expression of ideas, the department seeks to equip students with intellectual skills which have multiple uses in the larger society outside the university. [9] The History B.A. provides preparation for diverse fields: higher education, the law, federal, state, and local government, work in historical societies and museums, business, non-profits, and website development and research. [9]
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [11] Information about the accreditation of individual programs, schools and colleges is included in program descriptions in the Academic Programs Catalog. [11]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in History, Philosophy, and Sociology of Science
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in History, Philosophy, and Sociology of Science is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the nature of science and the role of science in society. Students in the program develop an understanding of the history of science, the philosophical foundations of science, and the social, cultural, and political dimensions of science and technology. The program prepares students for a variety of careers, including careers in science journalism, science policy, museum work, and education, and for graduate study in history, philosophy, sociology, and related fields.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Horticulture
Concentration: ['Horticultural Science', 'Landscape Design, Construction and Management', 'Sustainable and Organic Horticulture']
Description: The undergraduate Horticulture program integrates plant and soil science, entomology, pathology, technology and business management to prepare students to meet the challenges of an expanding multi-billion dollar-industry in intensively cultivated, high-value crops. [9] Horticultural crops are diverse, including annual and perennial species, food and ornamental plants and plants grown outdoors and in controlled environments. [9] The dynamic Horticulture program offers students hands-on and interactive learning experiences and opportunities inside and outside of the classroom. [9]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Business
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Business is for current Michigan State University students and is competitive and limited. Applicants are reviewed at the end of the semester in which they apply. Minimum criteria for consideration include the completion of 28 credits and specific core courses (WRA 101, STT 200, EC 201). [26, 30] Admission is primarily based on MSU cumulative GPA and a core GPA, with stated minimums for upcoming semesters (e.g., for Fall 2026, a 3.00 MSU Cumulative GPA and 3.00 Core GPA are required). [26] In addition to academic performance, the application requires a statement of professional goals, documented work experience, and extracurricular activities. [26]
Description: The undergraduate major in hospitality business blends hospitality business operations and fundamental areas such as accounting, finance, and marketing applied to hospitality business. [10] Substantial work experience in the hospitality industry is required for hospitality business majors. [10] The School of Hospitality Business prepares its students to enter management positions in lodging, food and beverage service, consulting, event planning, human resources, sales, information systems, marketing, as well as real estate investment management. [7] Graduates find opportunities in venues such as hotels, restaurants, resorts, casinos, cruise lines, clubs as well as in sports and entertainment. [7] The School of Hospitality Business was established in 1927, and in 1944 became the first hospitality program to be housed in a collegiate school of business. [7] Because of its unique industry-specific status within the Broad College of Business, The School of Hospitality Business curriculum is business-focused and driven by the hospitality industry. [7] Our graduates are equipped to face the challenges in this ever-changing industry, including operations, management, finance, accounting, marketing, human resources, information systems, law, production, facilities and emerging industry trends. [7]
Accredidation: Michigan State University is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. [12] The Eli Broad College of Business, which includes The School of Hospitality Business, is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). [17]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Biology
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive. First-year admission is based on your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, your ACT or SAT results (MSU is test-optional), and your leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. There are no minimum requirements. MSU strongly encourages a college preparatory curriculum in high school.
Description: The Human Biology major is designed for students who want a broad background in the biological sciences and plan to pursue careers in the health care professions. [5] It is an interdepartmental, undergraduate major in the College of Natural Science that serves students interested in careers in medicine, health sciences, and biomedical sciences. [2] The program integrates fundamental concepts from biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics/statistics, offering a comprehensive understanding of human biology and health. [11] Students are prepared to become leaders in providing equitable health care and addressing challenges in health, medicine, and the biomedical sciences. [2] The curriculum focuses on four main goals: connecting core scientific ideas to human health, applying critical thinking to solve problems, communicating effectively with diverse groups, and integrating scientific knowledge to address health inequities. [2] The major does not have formal concentrations but allows students to choose from a diverse list of selective courses to explore specific areas of interest. [7]
ScholarshipAmount: Varies

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Capital and Society
Requirements: The Bachelor of Arts in Human Capital and Society provides a general social science understanding of the complex nature of people and work. The program focuses on workforce education, training and development, laws governing employment and workplace rights, human decision-making and behavior in the labor market and workplace, and organizational strategies, policies and practices governing and influencing employee outcomes and performance. [2] The major requires a minimum of 36 credits, and students must graduate with approximately 120 total credits. [13] Required courses include HRLR 201, HRLR 313, HRLR 314, HRLR 315, HRLR 410, and HRLR 465(W). [12] Students must also complete a statistics course and an economics course. [12] The university's Tier II writing requirement is fulfilled by completing a designated 300-400 level course in the major. [13]
Department: School of Human Resources and Labor Relations
Description: Effective Fall 2024, the undergraduate major formerly known as Human Capital and Society was renamed Human Resources & Labor Relations. [7] The program focuses on the people side of business and prepares students for various professional careers related to employment and workplace strategies that shape the future of work. [8] It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of human capital in a global society, helping students develop critical thinking, problem-solving, social, emotional, and entrepreneurial skills to advance the well-being and success of working people, organizations, and communities. [8] Students learn to build motivating workplaces, foster diversity and inclusion, manage staffing and legal compliance, and analyze total rewards and labor market data. [7, 8]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Family Studies
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive, but there are no minimum requirements. MSU strongly encourages a college preparatory curriculum in high school. [3] At a minimum, this includes: Four years of English (composition and literature); Three years of mathematics (two years of algebra, one year of geometry); Three years of social studies (history, anthropology, economics, geography, government, political science, psychology or sociology); Two years of science (biology, chemistry, physics or earth science); Two years of a single foreign language. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Humanities - Prelaw
Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Humanities
Requirements: Michigan State University does not have a specific set of requirements for admission, but successful applicants typically have a strong high school curriculum, a quality senior year course load, and a sustained commitment to extracurricular activities. The university considers academic performance, the rigor of the high school curriculum, and standardized test scores (if submitted). There is no minimum GPA or class rank required.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interdisciplinary Neuroscience
Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Neuroscience is for students who wish to pursue a career in which a broad-based knowledge of the structure and function of the nervous system is necessary, including careers in research, education, healthcare or business. It is also intended for those students who seek admission to graduate study in neuroscience or health-related professional schools.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Interdisciplinary Studies in Social Science
Requirements: General application requirements are not explicitly detailed on a single page. For undergraduate admissions, MSU uses a holistic review process and is test-optional. For graduate admissions, applicants are advised to consult the specific requirements of their intended program.
Description: The undergraduate major in interdisciplinary studies in social science is designed for students who desire a broad-based education in the social sciences but who do not wish to limit their studies to a single discipline. The major provides a solid foundation for a wide range of careers and for advanced studies in various fields. Students have the opportunity to create a well-rounded and multifaceted liberal arts education by drawing on the diverse offerings of the social sciences. [3, 2] The program allows for the integration of common themes and diverse perspectives inherent in the social sciences. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Relations
Concentration: ['Political Economy and a given region', 'Social Relations and Policy and a given region', 'International Development and a given region']
Description: The major in international relations is an interdisciplinary, liberal arts program of study that focuses on the study of the world’s political, economic, and social systems. The major combines interdisciplinary, sequenced course work in James Madison College with a cross-college curriculum including, for example, foreign languages, economics, and history; a required field experience; and a senior seminar. The international relations major is designed to provide students with a sophisticated understanding of the relations between states and of the transnational problems and processes that affect all of humanity. The core curriculum provides a base of knowledge in history, the social sciences, and the humanities. Requirements for the major, including courses both in and outside the college, ensure that each student has a broad understanding of the international system, of the determinants of foreign policy, and of the dynamics of conflict and cooperation in the contemporary world. Students in the international relations major select one of three major fields: Political Economy and a given region, Social Relations and Policy and a given region, or International Development and a given region. All three fields are interdisciplinary and include course work within James Madison College as well as in other colleges.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Japanese
Description: The Bachelor of Arts degree in Japanese is designed to equip students with functional proficiency in the language, and cultural sensitivity to and factual knowledge about Japan. Education in another country is encouraged to provide students with firsthand experience of cultures superficially different from those to which they are accustomed, but are similar in many ways at the level of human interaction. Students who plan to complete the requirements for the major should consult an undergraduate advisor in Japanese.

Description: Uniquely, this program seeks to develop a high level of competency in jazz performance, and in compositional, scoring, and arranging skills. [7] It also strives to prepare individuals to understand the literature and historical and cultural context of jazz. [7] The Bachelor of Music in Jazz Studies is a professional degree program. [7] It includes the common core courses of all other Bachelor of Music degree programs and the shared objectives of musical literacy, development of aural skills, understanding of a broad repertoire, and attainment of analytical skills. [7]
Accredidation: The Michigan State University College of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM), 11250 Roger Bacon Drive, Suite 21, Reston, VA 20190-5248; Telephone: 703-437-0700.

[9] Whether focusing on political, sports, business, environmental, science, or international topics, the journalism major provides students with the professional preparation to serve society's needs. [9] Graduates are prepared to work in a range of traditional and innovative journalism-related occupations and platforms. [9]
Accredidation: The School of Journalism was one of the first journalism programs to be nationally accredited (1949), and one of the very few to be continuously accredited every six years since then, by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communication (ACEJMC). [7]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology
Requirements: Admission to Michigan State University is competitive. There are no minimum requirements, but students who are admitted have typically challenged themselves with a strong college preparatory curriculum. First-year admission is based on your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, and your ACT or SAT results (though MSU is test-optional). Your leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience are also considered.
Description: The major in kinesiology places emphasis on the multi dimensional study and application of physical activity to enhance health and well-being. Kinesiology explores not only anatomical, biological, biomechanical, and neurological aspects of physical activity; but also psychological, social-humanistic, and medical perspectives. The bachelor's degree program in kinesiology is designed to prepare students to enter a variety of fields associated with sport, exercise, and allied health, including professional graduate schools in medicine, physician assistant, nursing, physical therapy, occupational therapy, cardiac rehabilitation, athletic training, and chiropractic medicine. Students who graduate from this program often enter professional exercise science programs or graduate programs in the applied health sciences.

Description: The Bachelor of Science degree in Landscape Architecture is a professional degree program that prepares students for the practice of landscape architecture. The program is based on the mission of the School of Planning, Design and Construction to advance the knowledge, prepare innovative leaders, and support the practice of the built, natural and virtual environments. The program is structured to provide students with the opportunity to develop their abilities to analyze, plan, design and manage the land. It provides a foundation in the natural and social sciences as well as the arts and humanities. The goal of the program is to provide the educational experiences that will enable graduates to have productive careers in the private and/or public sectors and become licensed professional landscape architects.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree in Landscape Architecture is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB) of the American Society of Landscape Architects (ASLA).

Description: In order to assist students in planning a course of study, elective microbiology courses are organized by interest group (cell and molecular biology, immunology and medical microbiology, microbe biology, and microbial biotechnology) and students are advised in personal consultations to select a set of electives according to their interests. The objective of the Bachelor of Science degree program with a major in microbiology is to provide a broad foundation in science, with emphasis in microbiology. In order to increase the flexibility of the program, and to provide additional intellectual stimulation, students are encouraged to participate in tutored independent research for at least two, and ideally three or more, semesters. Thus, different emphases may be chosen by students intending to acquire technical competence in the field, to pursue graduate education in microbiology or another biological science, or to attain competence in a basic medical science preparatory to or in conjunction with professional study in human or veterinary medicine. This foundation provides the prerequisites for undertaking the basic courses in microbiology. In addition to the general degree requirements of the College of Natural Science, the undergraduate program in microbiology encompasses fundamental training in chemistry, mathematics, physics, and biology. [42] Independent research is available to both Honors College and other students, and often culminates with a report written in manuscript style by the student. This research may fulfill part of the department's capstone course requirement for the bachelor's degree with a major in microbiology.

Description: Neuroscience is the scientific study of the nervous system. Neuroscience seeks to understand the biological and chemical processes of the brain and nervous system. The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Neuroscience was established as a degree-granting program in 2012 and has since quickly become one of the most popular biological science degrees on campus. [3] The undergraduate major has its home in the Department of Physiology in the College of Natural Science since 2018, but there is also a coordinate major through the Lyman Briggs College. [3] This program is designed for students who wish to pursue a career where a comprehensive knowledge of the nervous system's structure and function is essential, including fields like research, education, healthcare, and business. [5] It is also intended for students seeking admission to graduate studies in neuroscience or to professional schools in health-related fields. [5]

Concentration: ['Biomedical and Molecular Nutrition', 'Public Health Nutrition', 'Global Nutrition and Health']
Description: There are several concentrations that Nutritional Sciences students can choose. Biomedical and Molecular Nutrition:Advances in human nutrition are revealing the importance of nutrition to human health and the mechanisms by which dietary components and their metabolites lead to health and wellness. In the biomedical and molecular nutrition concentration in the nutritional sciences major, you will study fundamental aspects of human nutrition that lead to careers in health, biomedical research, and academia. The curriculum is designed with an emphasis on the core sciences including chemistry, biochemistry, biology, physiology, and physics. You will also take courses covering more applied aspects of nutritional sciences to help provide a well-rounded education. This curriculum prepares students for careers in the biomedical sciences or for admission to medical, dental, optometry, pharmacy, or other graduate health programs. Public Health Nutrition: The public health nutrition concentration focuses on public health and nutritional epidemiology. You will be prepared for a career in community nutrition, health promotion and disease prevention, or in social policies that address the nutritional and health concerns of populations. The concentration provides knowledge in human nutrition and a foundation in core public health disciplines including epidemiology and biostatistics. Students also receive training in program planning, intervention, and evaluation. Global Nutrition and Health: The global nutrition and health concentration focuses on the international aspects of nutrition. The concentration provides students with knowledge of community nutrition, food security, sustainability, agricultural economics and policy, social justice, international development, and intercultural communication. The coursework also emphasizes program planning, intervention, and evaluation. Students who wish to combine this concentration with the Dietetics major can do so with additional coursework.

Description: The Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree with a major in Plant Biology is a liberal arts degree with a concentration in the plant sciences. It prepares students for ecologically or biotechnology oriented careers that are foundational to understanding the earth's biota and essential for supplying the world with food, fuel, and fiber. [4] The Plant Biology major is designed to give students a broad understanding of plant biology and/or fungal biology and prepares them to address some of the pressing global environmental challenges the world is facing today. [4] The program is also an excellent background for students wishing to enter graduate or other professional schools, including medicine, law or journalism. [4] While not formal concentrations, areas of emphasis can include Plant Ecology & Environment, Plant Biotechnology & Bioinformatics, or Plants & Microbes. [4]

This includes the study of American politics, political theory, comparative politics, and international relations. The program aims to develop students' analytical and communication skills and to prepare them for careers in government, law, business, non-profit organizations, and education. Students will learn about the theories and concepts of political science, as well as the methods used in political analysis. The curriculum provides a foundation for students who plan to pursue graduate studies in political science or related fields. Students are encouraged to develop a program of study that aligns with their interests and career goals. The department offers a range of courses that cover various aspects of politics and government.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Public and Professional Writing
Description: The bachelor's in Professional and Public Writing (P2W) provides students with an area of expertise in writing. Students develop advanced writing strategies and skills with an emphasis on rhetorical approaches and practices, such as writing anchored to audience, context, and purpose; writing attentive to community and cultural dynamics; and writing in consideration of public and professional trends and contexts. Students write in digital spaces, including web pages, social media, and content-management systems; write for and in diverse public and disciplinary communities and audiences; and edit and publish in a variety of public and professional contexts. The major prepares students for careers in professional editing and publishing, technical writing, information development, communications management, communications strategy, content management, and web and social media authoring. It also prepares students for graduate work in rhetoric, writing, technical communication, the teaching of writing, and the study of culture. Students interested in the Professional and Public Writing major should contact the Associate Chair and Director of Undergraduate Programs in the Department of Writing, Rhetoric, and Cultures. Students should work closely with the department academic advisor, the program director, and program faculty to shape a focus or theme in the major that fits their career interests and plans. Internships, management of writing projects, and development of a professional portfolio are all important aspects of student preparation for work in writing-related professions, in public or private settings such as nonprofits, small, and large corporations, or in graduate study.

This major is valuable preparation for those who intend to engage in research for public agencies, nonprofits or voluntary associations interested in the problems of government. A master's degree program concentrating in public policy is also available for advanced work in preparation for an executive career in these fields.

Requirements: First-year admission to Michigan State University is based on a comprehensive review of your academic performance in high school, the strength and quality of your curriculum, recent trends in your academic performance, your class rank, and your leadership, talents, conduct, and diversity of experience. [3] While there are no minimum requirements, a strong college preparatory curriculum is highly encouraged. [3] This includes four years of English, three years of mathematics, three years of social studies, two years of science, and two years of a single foreign language. [3] Each applicant is required to submit one essay (minimum 250 words, maximum 650 words). [16] The Bachelor of Science in Statistics program itself requires a minimum of 62 credit hours in approved coursework, which includes courses in mathematics, computation, and statistics. [4]
Description: A statistics major prepares students for careers in the modern, data-driven world. The program provides a solid background in mathematics and programming and builds upon this background with course work in probability, statistics, computational methods for data science and application of statistics and probability. [14] Students completing this major will be well prepared to design experimental studies, clean and analyze data, modify existing statistical methods guided by underlying theory, and effectively communicate results to stakeholders. [4] The Bachelor of Science degree in statistics requires greater science proficiency. [14] The degree requires 12 hours in an outside area of specialization, and while students can pursue a minor, it is not required. [3]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Studio Art
Description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts degree program with a major in studio art is a professional studio art program. Its emphasis is for students anticipating careers in the practice of art or design, or for students planning on graduate study in either field.

Fees: Tuition rates for 2026-2027 have not been released. Description: Supply chain management (SCM) integrates topics from manufacturing operations, purchasing, transportation and physical distribution into a unified program. The program offers integration among these critical, value-adding components to enhance global competitiveness.
CostPerCredit: Cost per credit information for 2026-2027 is not yet available. The per-credit hour rate is dependent on the student's level and residency status.
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. The Eli Broad College of Business offers scholarships specifically for supply chain management students.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Sustainable Parks, Recreation and Tourism
Requirements: As part of the undergraduate application for admission, each applicant is required to submit one essay with a minimum of 250 words and a maximum of 650 words. [2] Admission to Michigan State University is competitive, but there are no minimum requirements. MSU strongly encourages a college preparatory curriculum in high school. [6] At a minimum, this includes: Four years of English (composition and literature), three years of mathematics (two years of algebra, one year of geometry), three years of social studies, two years of science, and two years of a single foreign language. [6]
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources, Department of Community Sustainability
Description: The Sustainable Parks, Recreation and Tourism major combines an understanding of natural resource recreation and tourism with sustainability. It also effectively links theory with practice and community engagement. This major includes learning concepts of leisure, tourism, recreation and sustainability, as well as the operation of recreation delivery systems, policy, administration, management, planning and evaluation. [2] By combining a body of specialized professional knowledge with the study of natural, social, management and behavioral sciences, the program provides an opportunity for students to obtain a broad, interdisciplinary education which emphasizes a professional area of knowledge integrated with the tenets of sustainability. The major is designed to prepare students for professional positions related to the management and enjoyment of the outdoors. [1] Meeting people's outdoor leisure needs, enhancing the quality of life, and providing sustainable economic and social development are hallmarks of the major. [1, 2] Students in the Sustainable Parks, Recreation and Tourism major will acquire an understanding of natural resource recreation and tourism that integrates sustainability and effectively links theory with practice while engaging the community. [1]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre
Description: The MSU Department of Theatre offers you a personalized experience. We empower our students to think about a character from various vantage points, use technology to design and create new worlds, and examine the past in order to understand the present and influence the future. [2]
ScholarshipAmount: Awards may range from $500 to $5,000. [4]

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Urban and Regional Planning
Department: School of Planning, Design and Construction
Fees: For the 2025-2026 academic year, the average tuition and fees for an in-state first-year student are part of a total estimated cost of attendance. The average cost after aid for in-state students is approximately $22,034, and for out-of-state students, it is approximately $42,138, which includes tuition, fees, food, and housing. [31] Undergraduate students taking 12-18 credits are charged a flat rate, while those taking fewer than 12 are charged per credit hour. [31]
Description: The undergraduate program in urban and regional planning provides students with a basic understanding of environment-, economy- and society-related planning issues using scientific, social scientific or humanistic approaches. Students will learn the history of urbanism, the theory and principles of urban design, and the relevant legal and administrative policies and procedures. Students study the techniques of survey and research used in the analysis of the structure and growth of urban areas. They are involved in written and graphic communication. They recognize the contributions made by other disciplines concerned with the study of urban development, including politics, law, economics, social aspects, pollution control, natural resources and the interactions of human beings and nature. By developing systematic programs for the orderly and unified arrangement of urban physical structures, students focus their accumulated knowledge and skills on specific urban problems. The undergraduate program, which has been accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board, is designed to prepare majors to assume the responsibilities encountered in entry level professional planning practice.
Accredidation: The undergraduate program, which has been accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board, is designed to prepare majors to assume the responsibilities encountered in entry level professional planning practice.

ScholarshipType: The School of Planning, Design and Construction offers scholarships based on academic achievement, professional goals, and financial need. [3, 5, 10]

The degree contains core courses in biology, chemistry, physics, calculus and statistics. Students will complete a concentration encompassing several branches of modern zoology while allowing focused study in any one of those fields. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Accounting
Minor in Actuarial Science
Requirements: The Minor in Actuarial Science is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in any bachelor's degree program at Michigan State University. The student must complete 21 credits including: FI 311, FI 321, MTH 360, MTH 361, STT 441, STT 455, and either MTH 457 or STT 442. [1]
Description: The Minor in Actuarial Science, which is administered by the Department of Mathematics within the College of Natural Science, is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in any bachelor's degree program at Michigan State University. [2] This minor complements a number of major fields such as mathematics, statistics and probability, finance, and economics. [2] It is intended to prepare students for work in insurance companies, banks, investment firms, government work, hospitals and business firms where there is a need to weigh the financial consequences of risk. [2] The Minor in Actuarial Science prepares students for two of the examinations of the Society of Actuaries (SOA): Exam P/1 and Exam FM/2. [2] With the approval of the department that administers the student's degree program, courses that are used to satisfy the requirements for the minor may also be used to satisfy the requirements for the bachelor's degree. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in American Indian and Indigenous Studies
Description: The Minor in American Indian and Indigenous Studies, which is administered by the College of Arts and Letters, is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. [2] The minor is designed to help students understand American Indian and Indigenous cultures and identities and the place of Indigenous peoples and knowledge, historically and contemporarily, as well as to pursue cross-cultural diversity. [2] It draws on interdisciplinary research, teaching, and community engagement to examine these complex concepts and to respond to them thoughtfully. [2] Students who plan graduate study related to the humanities and social sciences or wish to pursue careers in education, social work, government, public health, law, non-profit management, museums, and cultural organizations that serve diverse populations, will find the minor engaging. [2]

ProgramName: Minor in Animal Science
Requirements: The Minor in Animal Science is available to all undergraduate students at Michigan State University. To be admitted, the student must have been admitted to Michigan State University. The student must contact the undergraduate advisor in the Department of Animal Science to apply for the minor. The application must be approved by the Department of Animal Science. To be awarded the minor, the student must complete at least 18 credits from a specified list of courses with a minimum grade-point average of 2.0.
Description: The Minor in Plant, Animal and Microbial Biotechnology is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in Bachelor of Science degree programs with majors in animal science, biosystems engineering, fisheries and wildlife, food science, forestry, horticulture, and plant, soil and microbial sciences. The minor provides the opportunity for students who are enrolled in biological science–related undergraduate programs to become familiar with the concepts, techniques, and issues related to modern biotechnology. The minor is designed for students who may be planning to pursue graduate study in biotechnology–related disciplines or who may be interested in careers with corporations or agencies for which a basic familiarity with biotechnology is a prerequisite.

ProgramName: Minor in Anthropology
Requirements: The Minor in Anthropology is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University other than the Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science Degree in Anthropology. Students who plan to complete the requirements of the minor should consult the undergraduate advisor in the Department of Anthropology. To complete the minor, a student must complete a minimum of 18 credits including: 9 credits from ANP 201, ANP 203, and ANP 206; 3 credits from a list of area courses; and 6 to 8 credits from a list of topical/analytical/methods courses. [1]
Description: Anthropology takes culture as its central object of study, giving students a framework for viewing culture in the context of the natural world and evolutionary processes. Anthropologists also study the organization of social life, as well as symbolic and ideological systems. [5]

ProgramName: Minor in Applied Development in International Agriculture and Natural Resources
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources
Description: This minor is available as an elective students are who enrolled bachelor's degree programs and is designed for students who have an interest in applied development in international agriculture and natural resources. It seeks to increase student understanding of global agriculture, particular agriculture-related problems and issues in developing and developed nations, and issues related to sustainability and stewardship of the Earth. Students who complete this minor will gain knowledge and experience relevant for careers in international agriculture, international development, and related fields.

ProgramName: Minor in Arabic
Description: The Minor in Arabic, which is administered by the Department of Linguistics, Languages and Cultures, will provide students the opportunity to acquire a core of basic knowledge of Arabic language and culture. The minor is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University other than the Bachelor of Arts Degree in Arabic. [3] With the approval of the department and college that administers the student's degree program, the courses that are used to satisfy the minor may also be used to satisfy the requirements for the bachelor's degree. [3]

ProgramName: Minor in Art History and Visual Culture
Requirements: The minor is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University other than the Bachelor of Arts Degree in Art History and Visual Culture. [3] Students who plan to complete the requirements for the minor must consult an undergraduate advisor in the Department of Art, Art History, and Design. [3] The student must complete 17 to 21 credits of specified coursework. [3]
Description: The Minor in Art History and Visual Culture, which is administered by the Department of Art, Art History, and Design, provides a minimum foundation in the field that may be used to supplement majors in other visual and cultural fields and enhance interdisciplinary expertise within other majors in the humanities. [4] The minor is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University other than the Bachelor of Arts Degree in Art History and Visual Culture. [4] With the approval of the department and college that administers the student's degree program, the courses that are used to satisfy the minor may also be used to satisfy the requirements for the bachelor's degree. [4] Students who plan to complete the requirements for the minor must consult an undergraduate advisor in the Department of Art, Art History, and Design. [4]
ScholarshipType: The College of Arts and Letters offers various scholarships for its students. [3, 8]

ProgramName: Minor in Arts and Cultural Management
Requirements: The minor is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. [2, 3] Students must complete 16 credits, which include 7 credits from core courses (ACM 271, ACM 471, ACM 496) and a minimum of 9 credits from a list of elective courses. [2] Students interested in the minor should consult the undergraduate advisor in the College of Arts and Letters. [2, 3]
Description: A comprehensive description of the program, its objectives, and what students will learn.The Minor in Arts and Cultural Management, which is administered by the College of Arts and Letters, provides students with a theoretical and practical training platform related to the management and advocacy of arts and cultural organizations and to dimensions of the industry known as artistic and humanistic entrepreneurship. [7] Students will engage with promotion, leadership, budgeting and e-strategies through participation in course work, experiential opportunities such as internships and volunteer positions, and other co-curricular activities that allow them to participate in critical analyses and production of arts and cultural management projects. [6] The minor is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. [6]

ProgramName: Minor in Asian Pacific American Studies
Description: The Minor in Asian Pacific American Studies, which is administered by the Department of History, focuses on the social and cultural history and contemporary issues relating to Asian Pacific Americans. This diverse group comes from varying class, ethnic, religious, and national backgrounds. The program incorporates an interdisciplinary approach to issues and populations in the United States, including exposure to current research, case studies, and contact with local communities. The minor is designed to complement a number of major fields and may be particularly engaging for students planning graduate study in the social sciences, ethnic studies, literature, media studies, or history. It may also interest those pursuing professional training in business administration and management, city and regional planning, counseling, education, law, library and information science, public health, and social welfare. [1]

ProgramName: Minor in Asian Studies
Requirements: General application requirements for Michigan State University are not centrally listed and vary by applicant type (freshman, transfer, graduate) and by specific program. Common components across most applications include a completed application form and submission of academic transcripts. For undergraduate applicants, essays are a part of the application. Graduate program requirements are determined by individual departments and may include letters of recommendation, a personal statement or statement of purpose, and a resume or curriculum vitae.
Description: The Minor in Asian Studies, which is administered by the Department of History, is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. Although the minor complements a number of major fields, students who plan graduate study related to Asia or who wish to pursue careers in government or with corporations in Asia may find the minor particularly appealing. With the approval of the department and college that administer the student's degree program, the courses that are in to satisfy the requirements for the minor may also be used to satisfy the requirements for the bachelor's degree. Courses taken in a Michigan State University Study Abroad program in Asia may be counted toward the minor with the permission of the Director of the Asian Studies Center and the student's advisor. The Minor in Asian Studies provides an opportunity for students to create a multidisciplinary specialty with Asia as the focus. The student's program of study for the minor must be approved in advance and in writing by the advisor for Asian Studies in Social Science.

Undergraduate minors at MSU generally do not have application requirements separate from university admission. Students can typically declare a minor if they are in good academic standing.
Description: The Minor in Coaching is designed to provide students with knowledge, skills, and expenses that will enable them to coach effectively and safely in school, community–youth, and adult sports programs. The Department of Kinesiology administers the minor. The educational objectives of the Minor in Coaching are for students to acquire: Knowledge and understanding of the growth and development of athletes. Knowledge and understanding of the medical, legal, psychological, social, biological, physical, theoretical, and technical aspects of coaching.

ProgramName: Minor in Beverage Science and Technology
Requirements: The Minor in Beverage Science and Technology is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. Students must complete 15 credits from a list of specified courses. [3]
Department: College of Agriculture and Natural Resources

Certain courses in this minor are only offered at off-campus wineries or breweries. The minor is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. The minor is administered by the Department of Food Science and Human Nutrition.

Minor in Bioethics

[5] Students are able to declare the minor upon completion of LB 240 by contacting the Lyman Briggs College. [5] The requirements for the minor are the completion of 1. The following course (2 credits): LB 240 Bioethics: Theories and Methods 2. One of the following courses (4 credits): LB 326A or LB 326B and 3. Complete 15 credits from at least four courses. [5]
Description: The Minor in Bioethics, which is administered by Lyman Briggs College, is available as an elective to students who are enrolled in bachelor's degree programs at Michigan State University. The minor is designed to prepare students to engage with theevolving ethical questions in biomedicine and to foster abilities to understand and question health care systems from a wide variety of intellectual viewpoints. The minor's interdisciplinary character promotes communication across disciplinary boundaries.

Minor in Biomedical Engineering
Minor in Biomedical Toxicology
Description: The Minor in Pharmacology Toxicology at Michigan State University is tailored for science-oriented students, aiming to introduce them to the fields of pharmacology and toxicology. [4] The program is designed to bolster career prospects and prepare students for admission into professional schools, including medical, veterinary, and pharmacy, as well as for graduate studies in biomedical disciplines and research-focused careers. [4] This undergraduate minor is offered as an elective for students enrolled in bachelor's degree programs. [4] The curriculum includes a variety of courses, from general surveys covering a wide range of drug classes to specialized courses on topics like drug safety, environmental toxicology, neuropharmacology, and tropical medicine. [6]
